body.statement: If \(h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\in\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B)\), then a rational vector \(\lambda\) satisfying \(\lambda B=h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\) exists and \(\tau_{x,y}(\theta)=F_{\lambda}(P_{\theta})\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_S\). The expression has a rational-coefficient numerator over a denominator dividing \(D_S(P)\), and \(D_S(P)>0\) throughout \(\operatorname{relint}(\Delta(S))\).
body.justification: Success must yield one evaluable formula valid everywhere on the face, not a numerical singleton test.
body.gap: Arithmetic-circuit invariant cuts and credal singleton computations are instance certificates; the common denominator and face-wide rational identity are the additional output here.
body.consumer: The functional can be evaluated, differentiated, audited symbolically, and passed to a support-scoped identification engine.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(\vartheta_j\) denote the column vector \(\theta_j|_{T_j(S)}\).  By the maximal-response-support theorem, all mass of \(\theta\in\Theta_S\) lies on \(T(S)\).  The definitions of the target tensor and the Kronecker matrix therefore give
\[
\tau_{x,y}(\theta)
=h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^m\vartheta_j\right),
\qquad
B\left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^m\vartheta_j\right)
=\bigotimes_{j=1}^m(B_j\vartheta_j).                            \tag{12}
\]
The matrix \(B\) and vector \(h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}\) have integer entries.  Membership in \(\operatorname{row}_{\mathbb Q}(B)\) is precisely solvability over \(\mathbb Q\) of
\[
\lambda B=h_{x,y}|_{T(S)}.                                     \tag{13}
\]
Multiplying (13) by the product mass vector in (12), and then using the district-signature-recovery theorem, gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{x,y}(\theta)
&=\lambda B\left(\bigotimes_j\vartheta_j\right)\\
&=\sum_{(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\in(\{0\}\cup S)^m}
\lambda[a_1,\ldots,a_m]\prod_{j=1}^m(B_j\vartheta_j)[a_j]\\
&=\sum_{(a_1,\ldots,a_m)\in(\{0\}\cup S)^m}
\lambda[a_1,\ldots,a_m]\prod_{j=1}^m t_j(P_\theta)[a_j]
=F_\lambda(P_\theta).
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{14}
\]

It remains to verify the global rational chart.  Every marginal probability appearing in \(t_j(P)\) is a sum of cells \(P(s)\), hence is a polynomial with integer coefficients.  In a fixed product term of \(F_\lambda\), a denominator associated with index \(i\) can occur only in the unique district containing \(V_i\).  If that term uses a supported cell \(a_j\) in that district, the denominator is one of
\[
P(V_{<i}=w),\qquad w\in S^{\le i-1};
\]
if the row is \(0\), no denominator is contributed.  Thus the denominator of each product term divides \(D_S(P)\).  Since \(\lambda\) is rational, bringing the finite sum to the common denominator shows that
\[
F_\lambda(P)=\frac{N_\lambda(P)}{D_S(P)}                       \tag{15}
\]
on the face interior, where \(N_\lambda\) is a polynomial with rational coefficients; cancellation may replace \(D_S\) by a divisor.

For each \(w\in S^{\le i-1}\), choose an \(s\in S\) extending \(w\).  If \(P\in\operatorname{relint}(\Delta(S))\), then
\[
P(V_{<i}=w)\ge P(s)>0.
\]
Every factor in \(D_S(P)\) is consequently positive (the empty-prefix factor is one), so \(D_S(P)>0\) throughout the relative interior.  This proves both the identifying equality and the asserted denominator property.
